title: Research a Public Domain
goal: Build a documented, passive picture of a public website or organization.
steps: Define the research question and scope.
Use search operators for public documentation and reports.
Review public robots.txt or sitemaps.
Inspect public DNS/RDAP records for domain context.
Check Certificate Transparency for historical certificate names.
Use web archives to compare important pages over time.
Triangulate important claims with independent public sources.
Record URLs, timestamps, observations, and confidence.
safety: Stay within public information; do not probe systems or bypass access controls.

title: Verify a Public Image
goal: Assess whether a public image is correctly attributed or contextualized.
steps: Preserve the image and source URL as observed.
Run a reverse-image search using the full image.
Try a distinctive crop when useful.
Compare candidate pages and publication dates.
Inspect visible signs, language, architecture, or geographic clues.
Check archived copies when dates conflict.
Separate observations from inferences.
State confidence and unresolved contradictions.
safety: Do not use image research to identify, track, or expose private people.

title: Research a Public Software Project
goal: Understand a public software project's history, documentation, and published interface.
steps: Start with the official repository or project site.
Read official documentation before secondary sources.
Search public issues and commits for distinctive terms.
Check releases and version history.
Compare public API or schema documentation.
Use archives when an important page changed.
Verify claims against maintainer sources.
Record exact versions and dates.
safety: Do not seek credentials, private repositories, or unauthorized access.
